cases.label: Cloud Optimization AI - Fleet Routing API
Managed Service For Microsoft Active Directory
Evenodd Same Winding
cases.trap: Two rings wound the SAME direction. Under evenodd the inner one is a hole. A converter that infers holes from opposite winding fills this solid.

cases.label: Nonzero Same Winding
cases.trap: Identical geometry to 01 but nonzero: NO hole, must render solid. Any converter that treats "nested ring" as "hole" fails one of these two.

cases.label: Unclosed Subpaths
cases.trap: Compound path whose subpaths have NO Z. SVG closes them implicitly for filling. Dropping the "duplicate" last point deletes a real vertex.

cases.label: Island In Hole
cases.trap: Three nesting levels: ring, hole, island inside the hole.

cases.label: Disjoint Nested Bbox
cases.trap: A wide U and a small square that sits inside the U's BOUNDING BOX but is geometrically disjoint. Bounding-box hole detection punches it out.

cases.label: Self Intersecting
cases.trap: Bowtie. evenodd leaves the crossing empty, nonzero fills it.

cases.label: Stroke Caps Joins
cases.trap: Every cap and join, plus a miter that exceeds the limit and must bevel. Excalidraw forces round caps/joins, so these only survive as outlines.

cases.label: Stroke Transform Scaling
cases.trap: Stroke width must be scaled by the element transform AND the viewBox fit. The three bars must end up visibly different thicknesses.

cases.label: Rounded Rect Variants
cases.trap: rx only, ry only, over-large radii that must clamp, a pill, and a rect that is genuinely a circle. A "big radius => ellipse" guess breaks these.

cases.label: Css Cascade
cases.trap: Cascade order: presentation attribute < stylesheet rule < inline style. Expected: left GREEN (class beats attribute), right BLUE (style beats class). A converter that only applies CSS when the attribute is missing shows red.

cases.label: Nested Clip And Mask
cases.trap: A clip and a mask nested on different ancestors. Only the INTERSECTION of the two should show. Taking the nearest one and stopping shows far too much.

cases.label: Luminosity Mask
cases.trap: Illustrator's luminosity-mask idiom: feFlood white behind a BLACK shape, so the mask means "everything except this circle". Read naively (black = hide all) the artwork disappears entirely.

cases.label: Mask Reveal And Hide
cases.trap: Painter-order mask: white square reveals, black circle then hides part of it, a second white square re-reveals an overlapping corner.

cases.label: Transforms
cases.trap: Nested transforms, rotate about a point, negative (mirroring) scale, and a raw matrix. Mirroring flips winding, which must not invert hole detection.

cases.label: Viewbox Offset
cases.trap: Non-zero, non-square, fractional viewBox origin. Hard-coding a 24x24 artboard or assuming origin 0,0 misplaces everything.
cases.expectedFailureReason: The shape is exact. The placement number comes from measuring a 0.5-unit hairline against a pixel grid. It sits just over the gate, and the gate stays where it is for everything else.

cases.label: Opacity
cases.trap: fill-opacity, stroke-opacity and inherited GROUP opacity, which multiplies rather than being inherited. Overlaps must composite, not replace.

cases.label: Gradients
cases.trap: Linear and radial gradients, plus a gradient referenced from a style attribute. All must flatten to a solid colour rather than vanish.
cases.expectedFailureReason: Excalidraw has no gradient paint. A gradient flattens to one averaged colour, and this number is how much colour the format cannot carry.

cases.label: Use And Symbol
cases.trap: <use> with its own x/y and transform, referencing both a plain shape and a group. Expanding it without honouring x/y stacks everything at the origin.

cases.label: Degenerate
cases.trap: Shapes that must be skipped without throwing, next to one that must still be drawn: zero size, zero radius, empty d, single moveto, NaN, 2-point fill.

cases.label: Unsupported Features
cases.trap: Everything the converter cannot represent. Nothing here should crash, and each item must be REPORTED rather than silently dropped.
cases.featureWarnings: dropped: <text> x1; dropped: <pattern> x1; approximated: <filter> x1; approximated: stroke-dasharray x1; approximated: marker x2; approximated: skew transform x1
cases.expectedFailureReason: One of everything the converter refuses to guess at. The requirement is that each feature is reported, not that it renders. A low score here would mean something was quietly approximated.

cases.label: Clip Objectboundingbox
cases.trap: clipPathUnits="objectBoundingBox": clip coords are FRACTIONS of the referencing element's geometry box, not user units. Read as user units the clip is a sub-pixel sliver near the origin and the shape disappears. The box here is deliberately offset and non-square so a wrong origin or a wrong aspect shows up immediately.

cases.label: Mask Contentunits Obb
cases.trap: maskContentUnits="objectBoundingBox": a 1x1 white rect means "reveal the whole object". Interpreted as user units it is a 1x1 sliver and the shape is erased. The black circle at 0.5,0.5 must punch out the centre.

cases.label: Mask Units Obb Tight
cases.trap: maskUnits="objectBoundingBox" with a TIGHT region. Unlike the -10%/120% default this genuinely crops, so skipping the region bound over-draws the right-hand half. Mask content is in user space (the default).

cases.label: Luminosity Filterunits Default
cases.trap: The luminosity-mask idiom relying on the filterUnits DEFAULT, which is objectBoundingBox (-10%/120%), not userSpaceOnUse. Miss it and the flood rect never appears, the mask becomes empty-minus-circle = empty, and the artwork vanishes entirely.

cases.label: Obb Degenerate
cases.trap: objectBoundingBox references whose box is unusable: a zero-height line, a group with no geometry at all, and a dangling clip-path id. The unit matrix is singular or absent, so the reference cannot be resolved. Nothing here may be silently deleted - over-draw and warn instead.

cases.label: Root Svg Presentation Attrs
cases.trap: Reported case. Paint declared on the root svg element, geometry in a bare child path with no fill of its own - the shape of most of SVG Repo, and of every Feather / Lucide / Tabler / Bootstrap / Heroicons outline icon. The inheritance walk in `getShapeStyle` used to stop *before* the root element, so `fill` here was never read, the path resolved to "no fill and no stroke", and the whole file converted to zero elements. NOTE: no literal svg start tag in this comment - the harness finds the root tag with a regex and would match the comment text instead.

cases.label: Implicit Default Fill
cases.trap: The SVG initial value of `fill` is black, not `none`. Nothing in the top row declares a fill, so all four shapes must render solid black. The converter used to treat "undeclared" and "explicitly none" as the same thing, which discarded all of it. The rows below are the controls: an explicit `fill="none"` really does mean no fill and must stay hollow, and `none` has to be recognised whatever its case. Opacity interactions are deliberately not exercised here; 16-opacity.svg owns that. This file scores a few percent of shape error against the browser even when perfectly correct: the ink is a handful of small shapes, so the one-pixel antialiasing ring around the circle is a large fraction of the total. What is being asserted is the fill decision, and the baseline gate is what holds it.
cases.expectedFailureReason: The fill decision is correct. The ink is a few very small shapes, so the one-pixel antialiasing ring around the circle is a large share of the total area.

cases.label: Ancestor Style And Class
cases.trap: Paint inherited from a <g> through `style=` and `class=`, not just through presentation attributes. Ancestors used to be read for attributes only, so `<g style="fill:...">` and `<g class="...">` contributed nothing and their children fell through to "no fill and no stroke". Nesting is included because the *nearest* declaration has to win, and because `style` outranks `class` on the same element.

cases.label: Artboard Spanning Artwork
cases.trap: Reported case. Line art whose silhouette touches all four edges of the artboard, on a 32-unit viewBox. The background-plate filter used to be two literal constants, 0.5 and 23.5, hard-coded for a 24x24 artboard but compared against root user-space coordinates. On this file 23.5 sits at 73% of the width, so the squirrel's body - one bridged 691-point ring - was classified as a background and deleted, leaving just the eye and one small island. Spanning the artboard is not what makes something a background; being solid is. This body inks 24.5% of its own bounding box, a rectangle inks 100% and a full ellipse 78.5%. NOTE: no literal svg start tag in this comment - the harness finds the root tag with a regex and would match the comment text instead.

cases.label: Clipped Circle
cases.trap: A circle and an ellipse, each cut in half by a clip path. Excalidraw's ellipse element is parametric - a box, not a point list - so there is nothing for a clip to intersect, and a converter that emits one anyway renders both shapes whole. The correct output is two half-discs with straight cut edges. The same shape written as a <path> is cropped correctly, so a whole-vs-half difference here is the ellipse route specifically.

cases.label: Class Style Rules
cases.trap: CSS stylesheet class rules declaring `fill: none`, `stroke`, `stroke-width` and `stroke-miterlimit`. Expected: transparent hollow rectangles with exact stroke width, not solid black boxes. A converter that ignores `fill: none` or `stroke-width` in CSS classes fills the rects solid black.
